contracts: One latest subscription per exact acknowledged renderer Owner; at most 128 renderer records, each with one high-water token and retirement task
Positive canonical signed-64 decimal client tokens are allocated once per invocation in the JS realm and persist across module re-evaluation; duplicate registration tokens are forbidden
Registration precedes initial inventory; uncommitted registration rolls back on cancellation/failure; stale release and late failed acknowledgement do not remove a replacement
Owner::retired registers a Notify waiter before its second atomic retired-state check; retirement wakes all waiters including registration races
Registry callbacks and destructors run outside registry locks; task captures weak registry; copied in-flight callbacks and late replies are fenced by frontend current-token and active checks
Tauri production Channels retain Webview/AppManager/managed Runtime; owner retirement removes the channel and breaks this transitive retention, with unit reference-cycle coverage
List/inspect/resolve use the shared owned blocking worker and publish successful snapshots even after the requesting async future is cancelled
Failed post-coordinator operations best-effort publish fresh inventory while retaining the original error; unreadable inventory is not fabricated
List, inspect, resolve and subscribe require an acknowledged current native renderer session; obsolete unsubscribe is harmless
Same-ID/same-generation pending inventory retains prior ready/attention presentation; changed generations invalidate it, and native resolution still claims/revalidates authority
